summary_note: The five withdrawn claims all held — no re-inflation detected in the body. The defects are concentrated in (a) the interaction term, which is promoted on an ordering the vault's own robustness sweep never tested and defended against a floor-effect challenge with an unargued assertion, and (b) two places where a confident headline sentence contradicts a caveat the report itself states 300 lines later.

findings.location: (iii) A. The boundary condition — the two-column pairing table, row 'Survives the floor-effect challenge': 'yes — unaffected' for the interaction; also Rank 1's 'Four reasons it is major rather than technical'
findings.issue: The report asserts without argument that the interaction η² is 'unaffected' by the floor-effect challenge, but a floor effect under perturbation is a candidate *generator* of exactly this interaction — if perturbation compresses all three surrogate cells toward a common floor, the surrogate gap shrinks under perturbation and stretches under gradient/CMA, which IS the measured interaction. The table's central asymmetry ('each survives exactly the challenge the other fails') therefore rests on an equivocation: the interaction escapes the floor effect only if it is read as the η² quantity, but the η² is the thing that fails the normalizer challenge; the normalizer-immune version of the interaction is the raw-units contrast, which is literally the same data as the 7/7 attenuation and inherits its confound.
findings.evidence: research/temp/findings-so-far.md, 'THE DIALECTICAL CHALLENGE' section: 'the interaction is real in raw units... Ens+CMA is ~2,600× worse than GP+CMA, while Ens+Pert is only 1.46× worse' — the raw-units interaction and the 7/7 raw-units attenuation are the same measurement. research/comparisons.md Tension 3 asserts the same asymmetry table without argument for the 'unaffected' cell.
findings.recommendation: Replace the bare 'yes — unaffected' with a scoped cell and add one or two sentences under Rank 1 conceding that a floor effect on perturbation would *produce* an interaction of this shape, so the floor-effect confound bears on the interaction's mechanistic interpretation too — what it does not touch is the interaction's *existence* and its significance in all four corners, which is a weaker and defensible claim. Also state plainly that the raw-units form of the interaction is not independent evidence from the 7/7 result, so the 'each survives what the other fails' pairing must be argued at the level of the η² quantity specifically, not the interaction in general.

findings.location: (iii) RANK 1 — 'It is the second-largest effect in every corner, ordered surrogate > interaction > optimizer without exception, at 4× to 33× the optimizer main effect' and reason (4) 'It cannot be dismissed as an operating-point artifact'
findings.issue: The ordering claim and the operating-point-immunity claim were never tested under the normalizer sweep the report itself relies on. The 33-combination sweep verified only that η²_surr > η²_opt (a main-effects ordering); the report's own Rank 5 concedes rank normalization 'consistently halv[es] the interaction' while η²_opt moves 'up to 3.4×'. A halved interaction (~0.075) against an η²_opt inflated 3.4× (0.036 → ~0.12) would invert the very ordering Rank 1 calls exceptionless. Reason (4) also directly contradicts section (i.M), which names the normalizer as 'a fifth operating-point coordinate the paper never names' — so the interaction is not immune to operating-point artifacts, it is untested against the fifth one.
findings.evidence: research/temp/interim-report-interaction-grounding.md, 'What would change this position': the locus names the rank/z-score recheck of the *interaction's direction* as its explicit falsifier and states 'I could not run this myself within this locus's remit/budget' — it remains an open dependency. research/temp/findings-so-far.md 'RESOLUTION of the normalization challenge': the 33 combinations are reported as preserving η²_surr > η²_opt only.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the ordering claim to 'under the paper's min–max normalizer' and insert a sentence stating that the interaction-versus-optimizer ordering was NOT among the quantities the 33-combination sweep verified, that rank normalization halves the interaction while inflating η²_opt up to 3.4×, and that confirming interaction > optimizer under at least one alternative normalizer is a prerequisite for the Rank 1 promotion. Soften reason (4) to acknowledge the fifth coordinate named in (i.M). Add this check to the Rank 9 experiment list as CHEAP.

findings.location: N6 Verdict, section D — 'It also yields a free result worth keeping: two crossed grids in the same subfield, decomposed the same way, disagree about which axis carries the variance... it is independent evidence for ground (1)'
findings.issue: The inference is a non-sequitur that contradicts the report's own conjunct (b). RaM's 0.577 sits on its *method* axis — nine bundled method identities which the report elsewhere insists are not a clean factor (CbAS and MINs 'genuinely aliased', Tri-Mentoring/PGS/Match-OPT 'layer method-specific machinery'). That axis is a mixture of model family, search paradigm and bespoke machinery, not model class. So 'swapping model class moves the dominant share' does not follow from it, and the claim that the two grids are 'decomposed the same way' about commensurable axes is a false parallel: RaM's loss-vs-method axes are not this paper's surrogate-vs-optimizer axes. This matters because the report offers it as independent evidence for ground (1) — one of only two grounds still standing after ground (2) was falsified.
findings.evidence: The report's own section D table, ground (2) row, and the N6 conjunct definitions in section A: '(a) surrogate model class varied across at least two genuinely distinct classes; (b) ... a bundled end-to-end method is not a clean optimizer level'. research/comparisons.md Tension 2 flags the η² was computed once with no second implementation.
findings.recommendation: Retract the 'independent evidence for ground (1)' clause and rewrite the 'free result' as the narrower thing it is: within RaM's own grid, a training-loss swap moves 2.7% of variance while the bundled-method axis moves 57.7% — which shows loss is a small factor there, not that model class is a large one. Note explicitly that RaM's method axis is not commensurable with this paper's optimizer axis, so the two grids cannot be said to 'disagree about which axis carries the variance'. Carry the once-computed caveat into this paragraph rather than leaving it only in the terminal section.

findings.location: N6 Verdict, section D table, ground (1) row — 'SURVIVES, now with domain support'; versus 'What I could not verify', section E
findings.issue: The report grades ground (1) confidently in the body while the terminal section concedes 'the ground currently rests on the uncertainty-quantification survey's taxonomy alone [11]' and that the AutoML/kernel-selection region 'was searched for crossed designs rather than for that taxonomic question'. After ground (2) was falsified on contact, ground (1) is load-bearing for an existential claim, and the reader of section D is not told its evidentiary base is one domain survey plus a comparator's convention.
findings.evidence: Draft's own terminal section E; research/comparisons.md Tension 2 calibration note: 'the AutoML / kernel-selection literature was not searched (could attack ground 1)'.
findings.recommendation: Add a clause to the ground (1) row (or immediately below the table) stating that its support is a single UQ taxonomy plus the comparator's convention, that no source was found treating model class and training objective as one factor but that the region was not searched for that specific taxonomic question, and that the stated criterion is proposed rather than sourced. Keep the verdict SURVIVES; make the base visible where the verdict is given.

findings.location: Opening, 'The severity of everything else must be split' — 'not one touches a number the paper computed' and 'Every quantitative claim checkable against a released artifact reproduced'
findings.issue: Self-contradicted twice by the report's own section (i.M). The tie count is described there as 'the only figure in the entire numeric sweep that does not reproduce' — that is a number the paper computed and it does not reproduce. And the η² bias finding means every published η² is upward-biased by +0.0099 to +0.0184 against the paper's own bootstrap artifacts, which touches the paper's central scalars. Calling the twelfth item 'an integer recount in a parenthetical' understates it in the same sentence that claims universal reproduction.
findings.evidence: Draft section (i.M): "'Five other cells tie it' should be six... It is the only figure in the entire numeric sweep that does not reproduce" and 'the bootstrap mean exceeds the point estimate in all four corners, by +0.0099 to +0.0184'. research/temp/synthesis-conflicts.md records the split as a designed reconciliation of drafts A and B.
findings.recommendation: Change the absolute 'not one touches a number the paper computed' to a precise statement: one computed integer does not reproduce, every published η² carries a small upward small-n bias the paper does not disclose, and no *direction* or *interval* the paper reports is overturned. That keeps the severity split doing analytical work instead of resting on an overstatement a reader can falsify from section M.

findings.location: Opening — 'the remaining pre-deadline hours belong entirely in related-work and scoping prose, and nothing needs re-running'
findings.issue: Stated with no bound, and the report's own terminal section F declares the bound: 'The bootstrap implementation, the ANOVA implementation and stats.py were not audited, so every numeric verdict in this report assumes they are correct' and 'no experiment was reproduced'. The 'NIL to results' verdict is conditional on an unaudited implementation, and the reader meets that condition 380 lines after meeting the verdict. Separately, 'nothing needs re-running' is contradicted by Rank 9 items 6 (mixed-effects, CHEAP-to-MEDIUM) and 7 (a depth sweep, MEDIUM), and by Rank 2's statement that the causal reading requires the disentangling analysis.
findings.evidence: Draft terminal section F; Rank 9 rows 6 and 7; Rank 2: 'The descriptive fact is solid; the causal reading is not.' research/comparisons.md Tension 1 calibration note: no mixed-effects model with task as a random effect was fitted.
findings.recommendation: Attach a short conditional to the 'NIL to results' sentence — that it holds against the paper's stored artifacts, whose bootstrap/ANOVA/stats implementations this audit did not audit and whose experiments it did not reproduce. And narrow 'nothing needs re-running' to 'nothing in deliverable (i) requires re-running an experiment', since deliverable (iii) recommends re-analyses and one new sweep.

findings.location: Section (i.D) — 'Ghasemipour et al. treat standard initialization-seed-diversified ensembles — the audited construction — as the reliable reference' versus section (i.I) — 'Their entire scope is one surrogate class, Q-ensembles... They never compare across distinct model families'
findings.issue: The same source is scoped two incompatible ways depending on which direction it cuts. Section I criticises the paper for over-extending Ghasemipour beyond offline-RL Q-ensembles; section D then extends Ghasemipour exactly that far, using it as a counterweight about regression surrogate ensembles. If the narrow scoping in I is right, the counterweight in D is the same over-extension the report calls a mandatory fix.
findings.evidence: Draft sections (i.D) and (i.I); research/temp/source-tensions.json tension 1 lists Ghasemipour on side_a while its resolution notes the source is an offline-RL study.
findings.recommendation: Add a scoping clause where Ghasemipour appears in section D — that the source is offline-RL Q-ensembles and its 'reliable reference' status transfers to a regression surrogate only by argument — and cross-reference section I so the two scopings are visibly the same. Do not delete the counterweight; the point survives, it just needs the same discipline the report applies elsewhere.

findings.location: (iii) RANK 1, 'Two qualifications must travel with it' — 'on Design-Bench η²_inter is only 0.006–0.041 and subordinate to η²_opt there — consistent rather than contradictory, since where surrogate cells are frozen neither main effects nor interactions involving them can appear'
findings.issue: The report explains away its single strongest piece of disconfirming evidence for the interaction with a mechanism that appears nowhere in the evidence base and was never tested. Frozen cells are documented only on TF-Bind-8 and Ant, a subset of the Design-Bench tasks, and Design-Bench's own η²_opt is 0.05–0.20 there — i.e. the axes are demonstrably not all flattened, which is what the frozen-cell story would predict. Presenting a conjecture with 'consistent rather than contradictory' converts a live boundary condition into a resolved one.
findings.evidence: research/temp/interim-report-interaction-grounding.md states the Design-Bench boundary condition and offers no frozen-cell explanation: 'an order of magnitude below the synthetic grid's 0.146–0.165... Any promotion must be scoped explicitly to the synthetic grid.' Draft section (i.N) locates frozen cells on Ant and TF-Bind-8 specifically.
findings.recommendation: Demote the frozen-cell clause from an explanation to a hypothesis — state that frozen cells are a candidate explanation, that they are documented on only some Design-Bench tasks, that Design-Bench's nonzero η²_opt is in tension with a general flattening account, and that the interaction is currently a synthetic-grid result whose failure to generalise is unexplained. That is the honest version and it costs the recommendation nothing.

findings.location: (iii) RANK 1 — 'Three independent routes reached this finding, none prompted by the others; convergence on a quantity the paper prints four times and never discusses is itself a finding'
findings.issue: Convergence is offered as corroboration when it is three observers reading the same conspicuous unreported cell in the same artifact table — the same signal detected three times, not three independent lines of evidence. The orchestrator's own notes flag precisely this pattern ('I predicted four of four early findings correctly... a warning sign, not a comfort') as a reason to distrust convergence, and the report reproduces the convergence claim without that discount.
findings.evidence: research/temp/orchestrator-notes.md lines 71 and 252–253: 'Four for four on the ones that have returned. That is a warning sign, not a comfort' and 'the most likely failure mode is inheriting my errors, not making new ones.' research/comparisons.md, 'The convergence worth stating separately'.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the convergence sentence: three routes examined the same artifact table, so convergence establishes that the number is hard to miss once looked for, not that it is independently corroborated. The substantive case for Rank 1 rests on the four-corner intervals and the DOE argument, not on how many readers noticed it — say so and let the weaker warrant go.

findings.location: Opening, paragraph beginning 'The largest recoverable value is a pair of positive findings' — 'a 7-of-7 attenuation of the surrogate gap under weak search sitting in the supplement's raw-units table'
findings.issue: The executive summary presents the 7/7 attenuation as a recoverable positive finding with no mention of the floor-effect confound, while Rank 2 states the causal reading 'is not established, and this audit's own test went against it'. A reader who reads only the opening — the most-read part of an audit — takes away a positive result the body says must be posed as a question rather than asserted. This is the mildest form of the re-inflation the brief warns about.
findings.evidence: Draft Rank 2: 'The one task where perturbation is the grid's best optimizer — Styblinski-5D — is the task with the weakest attenuation (14.3%). That is exactly what a floor effect predicts.' research/comparisons.md Tension 3 records the confound as live.
findings.recommendation: Add a half-clause to the opening — that the raw-units attenuation is a solid descriptive fact whose causal reading carries a live floor-effect confound and should be folded in as a question the paper poses and tests. One clause; it keeps the summary consistent with Rank 2.

findings.location: Section (i.D) — 'Net: "this specific σ construction has a known calibration caveat," never "MSE ensembles are broken."'
findings.issue: The report closes with a settled 'Net:' where the vault's own resolution records the thread as genuinely unresolved: Ghasemipour treats this exact construction as reliable while Lakshminarayanan flags it, and nobody has reconciled the two directly. Asserting a net verdict over an unreconciled disagreement is the losing-side-unengaged pattern, in the one place the report is otherwise exemplary.
findings.evidence: research/temp/source-tensions.json tension 1 resolution: 'Note the one genuinely unresolved thread: Ghasemipour treats this exact construction as reliable while Lakshminarayanan flags it, and nobody has reconciled that directly.'
findings.recommendation: Append one sentence to the 'Net:' noting that the reliability of the MSE-plus-empirical-variance construction is itself unreconciled in the literature — one source treats it as the reliable reference, another flags it as the weaker of two options — which is an additional reason to scope the paper's claim to its own grid rather than to arbitrate.

findings.location: (iii) RANK 3 — 'it is not a defence — it is a contribution to an established line' alongside 'Lucic et al., verbatim, "bad models can outperform good models given enough computational budget"... That is the paper's own finding, stated at NeurIPS 2018'
findings.issue: Rank 3 calls the budget result the clearest under-stated finding carrying the strongest evidence in the paper, and then concedes in the same paragraph that its core sentence was stated at NeurIPS 2018 by a paper already in the bibliography. The report never reconciles these: if Lucic stated it, the finding is a confirmation on a new axis rather than an under-stated contribution, which changes how the paper should frame it.
findings.evidence: Draft Rank 3, citing [34] and [65]; the COCO §3.5 budget-dependent-benchmarking apparatus is described as 'a decade-old' methodological category.
findings.recommendation: Add a sentence resolving the tension in the paper's favour but honestly: the qualitative statement is Lucic's and the methodological category is COCO's, so the paper's contribution is the *quantified* version on the surrogate-versus-optimizer axis with disjoint intervals and a ranking flip — a measured instance of a named phenomenon, which is what it should claim rather than novelty.
